This policy defines which document takes precedence in cases of disagreement or temporal inconsistency.

name: FirstUK

name: Authority Order for Document Hierarchy
description: A formal governance framework establishing the hierarchical authority of different document types and regulatory sources within the organization. The framework prioritizes applicable law and regulator direction at the highest level, followed by board-approved policies, standard operating procedures, operational guides, customer communications, and reference materials. Lower-authority documents may explain requirements but cannot weaken higher-authority mandates.
context: For the same subject, apply the highest applicable authority first
Applicable law, regulator direction, and regulatory circular requirements
Board-approved policy and risk appetite statements
A lower-authority document may explain how to carry out a requirement, but may not weaken a higher-authority requirement
An explicit supersession controls from its effective date
decision_topic: hierarchical authority framework for policy and regulatory compliance
rationale: establish clear precedence for conflicting requirements across regulatory, policy, procedural, and operational documentation
authority_hierarchy: Applicable law, regulator direction, and regulatory circular requirements
Board-approved policy and risk appetite statements
Approved operational guides and training manuals
Reference material, FAQs, and descriptive system documentation
key_constraint: lower-authority documents may not weaken higher-authority requirements
supersession_rule: explicit supersession controls from its effective date

name: Status Vocabulary
description: A reference table defining four document statuses (Draft, Active, Superseded, Withdrawn) and their permitted operational use. This vocabulary governs how documents are classified and applied in decision-making and compliance contexts.
context: Status Vocabulary
Draft | Not approved for operational use | Context only; do not rely on it for a decision
Active | Approved and currently effective | Apply if it governs the question date
Superseded | Replaced by a named later document | Use only for historical questions before replacement
Withdrawn | No longer valid and not replaced | Do not use as operating guidance
decision_topic: Establishment of document status classification framework

name: Document Reliance Risk
description: The risk that draft or withdrawn documents are applied operationally when they should not be, leading to non-compliance or incorrect decision-making. The vocabulary explicitly restricts reliance on draft documents to context only and prohibits use of withdrawn documents as operating guidance.
context: Draft | Not approved for operational use | Context only; do not rely on it for a decision
Withdrawn | No longer valid and not replaced | Do not use as operating guidance
stated_prohibitions: Do not rely on Draft documents for decisions
Do not use Withdrawn documents as operating guidance
Do not apply Superseded documents after replacement effective date
control_mechanism: Status classification and permitted use restrictions

name: Decision Rule Framework for Document Authority and Supersession
canonical_name: Decision Rule Framework for Document Authority and Supersession
key: decision rule framework for document authority and supersession|GOVERNANCE_DECISION|banking.risk_governance
description: A formal governance framework establishing the precedence and application rules for determining which documents are in force on a given date. The framework prioritizes explicit supersession over version-number comparison and applies an authority order when active documents of equal standing overlap. Conflicts between equal-authority sources are to be identified, attributed, and escalated rather than resolved by invention.
context: Establish the decision or event date.
Apply explicit supersession before a general version-number comparison.
Apply the authority order when active documents overlap.
If active sources of equal authority disagree and no resolution is recorded, identify and attribute the conflict; escalate rather than invent a rule.
decision_topic: Framework for resolving document authority conflicts and supersession rules
rationale: Establish systematic approach to document authority determination, supersession application, and conflict escalation
related_action_items: Document Authority Analysis and Conflict Escalation
framework_steps: Establish the decision or event date
Identify documents in force on that date
Apply explicit supersession before general version-number comparison
Apply the authority order when active documents overlap
Identify and escalate conflicts where equal-authority sources disagree with no recorded resolution
Record documents considered and basis for decision

name: Document Authority Analysis and Conflict Escalation
canonical_name: Document Authority Analysis and Conflict Escalation
description: An ongoing governance obligation to analyze active documents in force on a decision date, apply the authority order framework, and escalate any conflicts between equal-authority sources that cannot be resolved by explicit supersession or version comparison. The process requires recording all documents considered and the basis for each decision.
context: Record the documents considered and the basis for the decision.
If active sources of equal authority disagree and no resolution is recorded, identify and attribute the conflict; escalate rather than invent a rule.
action_description: Analyze document authority, apply supersession rules, resolve overlapping documents by authority order, and escalate unresolved conflicts between equal-authority sources
triggered_by: Decision Rule Framework for Document Authority and Supersession
success_criteria: Explicit supersession rules applied before version-number comparison
Authority order applied when active documents overlap
Unresolved conflicts identified and escalated rather than invented
All documents considered and decision basis recorded
